history.period: Ancient (Shakta pitha tradition); Koch-era reconstruction 16th century (verify exact chronology)
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the ancient Shakti pitha on the hilltop at Tukura Pt-II near Matia, Krishnai, Goalpara district, Assam. The name derives from the Assamese 'tukura' (fragment/piece) - a portion of Goddess Sati's body is believed to have fallen here during Shiva's tandava. The temple complex includes the main Sati shrine and a secondary Shiva shrine; local accounts trace it from a natural cave shrine through Koch-period rebuilding (a 1565 rock inscription records Koch patronage; the Darrang Rajavamsavali recounts Biswa Singha discovering it in jungle ruins). CSV ERROR: the 'state' column holds the town name; the real state is ASSAM. Site is at Tukura near Krishnai/Matia on NH 37, roughly 18-20 km from Goalpara town (verify distance); nearest railhead and exact opening hours unverified.

town_description: Goalpara is a district-headquarters town in lower Assam on the south bank of the Brahmaputra, set among low hills; the surrounding area is known for its Shakti shrines (including the Mahamaya Dham in adjoining Kokrajhar district) and for the Tukreswari hill shrine near Krishnai.
